title: CS2 World Bundle warning record (contract section 10)
description: One line of warnings.jsonl (JSON Lines): something the producer could not do, said out loud, so that a missing object is explicable rather than mysterious. A CONSUMER MAY IGNORE THIS FILE ENTIRELY — but it is schema-validated all the same, because it is also how a producer DECLARES a gap it could not close: an assetId referenced by instances.jsonl with no .glb behind it is normally invalid, and declared here it validates as a note instead, so the objects still land in the right places behind a stand-in. That amnesty is keyed on 'assetId' and 'reason', so a line the validator cannot read silently stops excusing anything.

kind.description: What kind of thing is missing. KINDS ARE OWNED PER PASS and each pass rewrites only its own, so a stage re-run cannot erase another stage's declarations: the instance pass owns 'prefab' and 'instance', the mesh pass 'mesh'/'material'/'texture', the lane pass 'lane', the network pass everything prefixed 'network', and the terrain pass everything prefixed 'terrain' ('terrainFine': the fine cascade raster was wanted and could not be captured, added 2026-08-16). The network prefix is load-bearing — a network warning names a cross-section piece that is NOT an assetId in meshes/, so filing it as 'mesh' would let the next mesh rip delete it.

assetId.description: The id or name a consumer would have looked for. Usually an assetId in the sense the mesh layers use it, but not always — the network stage files a whole-directory warning as 'networks/', so this is a free string rather than a filesystem-safe id.

id.description: The would-be record's 'id' instead of an assetId, for the two kinds that name an ENTITY rather than an asset ('instance' and 'lane'): an entity the simulation removed mid-rip no longer resolves to a prefab to ask for.

reason.description: Why it is not there, in prose. Read it: a declared assetId may EXIST BUT BE INCOMPLETE — a geometry asset whose meshes could not all be read still writes the .glb from what survived, with a 'partial: …' reason here, because the meshes of one asset draw together (section 6) and an incomplete file is invisible from the file alone. Presence of a warning therefore does not imply absence of the file.
